From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Finnic *puhudak (“to blow”) (compare Estonian puhuma),[1] from Proto-Uralic *puše- (“to blow”) (compare Northern Sami bossut, Western Mansi [script needed] (put-)).[2] Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).[3][4]

The semantic shift from “to blow” to “to speak” is found only in Finnish (and rarely in Karelian), unless Proto-Mordvinic *pəškaďəms (“to accost, speak (to), address”) derives from the same root[5]. It may have developed via a sense “to cast a healing spell”, which is found also in some other Finnic languages. Note that the Finnic languages have multiple unrelated words for “to speak, talk” (Estonian rääkima, Ingrian läätä, Karelian paissa ~ Livvi paišta ~ Ludian pagišta ~ Veps pagišta, Livonian rõkāndõ, Võro kõnõlõma, Votic pajatta).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpuhuɑˣ/, [ˈpuɦuɑ̝(ʔ)]
  • Rhymes: -uhuɑ
  • Syllabification(key): pu‧hu‧a
  • Hyphenation(key): pu‧hua

Verb

[edit]

puhua

  1. (intransitive, rarely transitive) to speak, talk (communicate with one's voice)
    Nuorin lapseni opettelee vasta puhumaan.
    My youngest child is just learning to speak.
  2. (intransitive) to speak, talk [with elative ‘about, of’ and allative ‘to’] (communicate, discuss, converse; usually by speaking or with one's voice)
    Me puhuimme ainakin tunnin.
    We talked for at least an hour.
  3. (intransitive) to speak (deliver a speech)
    Synonym: pitää puhe
    Matti on lupautunut puhumaan illan juhlassa.
    Matti promised he would speak at tonight's event.
  4. (transitive, usually atelic) to speak (be able to communicate in a language)
    Puhutko englantia?
    Do you speak English?
  5. (poetic) synonym of puhaltaa (“to blow”)
